KEY MESSAGE 1...Periods of rain and gusty winds through this evening.

A sharp mid level trough will advance east across the Great Lakes 
today through tonight. An associated surface low will steadily 
deepen through the period as it moves through southern Ontario 
province today, then northeast down the Saint Lawrence Valley 
tonight to the Canadian Maritimes Saturday. This system has captured 
a plume of deep moisture, with PWAT values briefly rising to around 
1.75" in the warm sector this morning.

A period of strong isentropic upglide and moisture transport will 
move northeast across the eastern Great Lakes early this morning as 
a warm front races northeast across the area. Ascent across the warm 
front will be enhanced by a 55+ knot low level jet, and continue to 
support a few periods of rain. The cold front will quickly follow, 
moving southeast across the area this afternoon and bringing another 
period of low level convergence and additional showers. DPVA ahead 
of the mid level trough and strong right entrance region jet 
dynamics will lag behind the passage of the cold front, allowing for 
periods of light rain to continue this afternoon and evening even 
after the surface cold front passes by.

Elevated instability may support a few isolated weak thunderstorms 
this morning. A few more scattered thunderstorms may develop along 
the cold front late morning through early afternoon from the 
Southern Tier into the Finger Lakes along the advancing cold front 
as modest surface based instability develops. If these storms 
materialize they may produce gusty winds, with a better risk of 
severe thunderstorms well southeast of our area where greater 
instability will develop.

Rainfall amounts will vary widely across the area, generally ranging 
from 0.25" to 1.0". Terrain will play an important role given the 
strong boundary layer flow, with downslope areas of the Lake Erie 
shore and Genesee Valley likely on the low end of the range, while 
higher terrain is more likely to be on the higher end of the range 
from upslope enhancement. There may be a few small areas that exceed 
1.0" if embedded convection develops.

Finally, it will be quite windy today as a strong 55+ knot low level 
jet propagates across the eastern Great Lakes. A brief window of 
downslope winds will continue early this morning along the Lake Erie 
shore, and later this morning north of the Tug Hill Plateau. The 
setup for downslope winds is not ideal, with a weak inversion and 
SSW flow not directly perpendicular to the terrain barriers. Given 
the marginal setup, expect wind gusts of up to 40 mph in downslope 
areas this morning, and 25 to 35 mph elsewhere. A brief period of 
stronger winds will also develop northeast of Lake Erie late morning 
through mid afternoon as the cold front crosses the area. Once again 
this setup it not ideal, with most of the strong winds aloft in the 
warm sector where lapse rates are poor. Boundary layer winds will 
quickly drop off later this afternoon following the cold frontal 
passage when lapse rates steepen. Expect peak gusts of up to 40 mph 
northeast of Lake Erie today.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Much colder tonight through Saturday night with a 
few wet snowflakes possible early Saturday morning.

Strong cold advection will develop tonight in the wake of the 
departing low, with 850 mb temperatures dropping into the -5C to 
-8C range by Saturday morning. The cold air aloft will support 
increasing lake induced instability overnight with a brief lake 
response, but short NNW fetch and a rapidly drying synoptic scale 
airmass will keep lake effect muted and brief. Lake effect and 
upslope rain showers will develop southeast of the lakes tonight, 
with a few wet snowflakes possibly mixing in very late tonight 
through early Saturday morning before the lake effect showers 
quickly end by late morning. The best chance of a few snowflakes 
will be across higher terrain, but no accumulation is expected.

The coldest airmass of the fall season so far will arrive for 
Saturday, with highs only in the 40s areawide, and even upper 30s 
across the highest terrain despite some afternoon sunshine. 
Temperatures will drop back into the lower 30s on the lake plains 
and 20s well inland Saturday night, with frost/freeze conditions 
likely.

KEY MESSAGE 3...An extended period of dry and warmer weather begins 
Sunday and lasts most of next week.

High pressure will drift from the Ohio Valley to southern New 
England Sunday, with southwesterly return flow quickly removing the 
brief shot of colder air. Temperatures will rebound into the 55 to 
60 degree range by afternoon following the cold start.

A strong ridge surface and aloft will then take up residence early 
next week across much of the central and eastern CONUS, while a slow 
moving cutoff low remains parked off the Carolina coast much of the 
week. This pattern will support dry weather most, or even all of
